title: Lockstep test pins a test-local duplicate list, never the production terminal_statuses const it claims to guard
evidence:
server/test/application/application_detail_handler_test.gleam:593: `pub fn terminal_statuses_lockstep_with_shared_truth_test() {
  let terminal = [
    "form_completed",
    "manual_recorded",
    "unreachable",
    "refused",
    "objected",
    "partial",
    "failed",
    "completed",
  ]` — versus the production list it names, server/src/application/application_detail_handler.gleam:1286: `const terminal_statuses: List(String) = [
  "form_completed",
  "manual_recorded",
  "unreachable",
  "refused",
  "objected",
  "partial",
  "failed",
  // v2-reserved voice terminal — harmless to include.
  "completed",
]` (private const, never imported or read by the test; consumed at application_detail_handler.gleam:1454 `let terminal_entries = case list.contains(terminal_statuses, status) {`).
detail: The test asserts the shared fn against its own hardcoded copy. The production list that build_lifecycle_entries uses is unreferenced, so an edit to it (add/remove a status) passes CI — the claimed lockstep guarantee doesn't bite on the production side.
recommended_fix: Export the const (or a pub fn returning it) and have the test iterate the production list, asserting every entry is_terminal_status and vice-versa for non-entries.

title: Second server-side terminality list survives in trigger.gleam, unpinned by any AR-RC13 guard layer
evidence:
server/src/reference_checks/trigger.gleam:1153: `fn is_terminal(status: String) -> Bool {
  list.contains(
    [
      "form_completed",
      "unreachable",
      "refused",
      "objected",
      "manual_recorded",
      "failed",
      "completed",
      "partial",
    ],
    status,
  )
}` used at trigger.gleam:1117: `          row.ref_slot == slot
          && row.owner_label == primary_owner
          && !is_terminal(row.status)` (inside find_live_row_for_slot, 'Exported for the RC4.3 substitute path's successor read').
detail: The amendment claims terminality has ONE home (shared is_terminal_status), but this private 8-entry list re-derives it. Neither the lockstep test, the truth-table test, nor the hooks lint reads it; drift would silently change which row the substitute successor read treats as live.
recommended_fix: Replace the local list with shared_reference_call.is_terminal_status(status_from_string(status)), and extend the lockstep test to cover this call site (or delete the fn).

title: Same-instant attempts in mixed formats split into two cadence batches — the new pin covers ordering, not grouping
detail: Two attempts of one send with the same instant in space-form and T-form become two batches (cycle 0 + cycle 1), rendering mislabeled "Invitation sent" plus "co-nudge" lines for a single send; the new test cannot catch it.
recommended_fix: Normalise at inside group_attempts_by_at (group on the normalised key), or add a same-instant mixed-format fixture asserting the two entries share one batch label.

title: Em-dash lint has two verified false-negative paths: odd escaped-quote parity and log-call lines
detail: A user-facing string containing an odd number of escaped quotes flips the scanner's in-string state and hides a later em-dash; any log call sharing the line exempts it. Both bypass the CI gate for the ban.
recommended_fix: Treat backslash-escaped characters as non-delimiters in the scan (as strip_comments already does), and scope the log-call exemption to the argument span instead of the whole line.

title: Hooks lint only detects hook-governed actions as the FINAL element of a list literal — multi-element lists evade
evidence:
scripts/lint_refcheck_hooks.py: `            # construction shape only: identifier immediately followed by `]`
            marker = action + "]"
            if marker not in line:
                continue`. Verified by simulation against the current panel shapes: the line `'Unreachable -> [RefcheckTakeOver, RefcheckSubstitute]'` trips only for RefcheckSubstitute — `RefcheckTakeOver]` never occurs, so a take-over re-derived as a non-final element passes silently.
detail: The historical RC4.3-r1 shape is caught only because substitute sits last and take-over also appears as a single-element list elsewhere; a status-derived menu listing take-over first (or building the list via a helper) evades the gate.
recommended_fix: Match the bare identifier at word boundaries (keep the pattern-arm `->` exemption) and run the enclosing-hook-case check on every occurrence, not only the `action]` shape.
